title: 2012年真题 · Text 1
passage:
Homework has never been terribly popular with students and even many parents, but in recent years it has been particularly scorned. School districts across the country, most recently Los Angeles Unified, are revising their thinking on this educational ritual. Unfortunately, L.A. Unified has produced an inflexible policy which mandates that with the exception of some advanced courses, homework may no longer count for more than 10% of a student's academic grade.

This rule is meant to address the difficulty that students from impoverished or chaotic homes might have in completing their homework. But the policy is unclear and contradictory. Certainly, no homework should be assigned that students cannot complete on their own or that they cannot do without expensive equipment. But if the district is essentially giving a pass to students who do not do their homework because of complicated family lives, it is going riskily close to the implication that standards need to be lowered for poor children.

District administrators say that homework will still be a part of schooling; teachers are allowed to assign as much of it as they want. But with homework counting for no more than 10% of their grades, students can easily skip half their homework and see very little difference on their report cards. Some students might do well on state tests without completing their homework, but what about the students who performed well on the tests and did their homework? It is quite possible that the homework helped. Yet rather than empowering teachers to find what works best for their students, the policy imposes a flat, across-the-board rule.

At the same time, the policy addresses none of the truly thorny questions about homework. If the district finds homework to be unimportant to its students' academic achievement, it should move to reduce or eliminate the assignments, not make them count for almost nothing. Conversely, if homework matters, it should account for a significant portion of the grade. Meanwhile, this policy does nothing to ensure that the homework students receive is meaningful or appropriate to their age and the subject, or that teachers are not assigning more than they are willing to review and correct.

The homework rules should be put on hold while the school board, which is responsible for setting educational policy, looks into the matter and conducts public hearings. It is not too late for L.A. Unified to do homework right.
passage_zh:
家庭作业从来都不太受学生欢迎,甚至许多家长也不喜欢,但近年来它尤其遭到鄙视。全国各地的学区,最近的是洛杉矶联合学区,正在重新思考这一教育惯例。不幸的是,洛杉矶联合学区制定了一项不灵活的政策,规定除了某些高级课程外,家庭作业在学生学业成绩中所占比重不得超过10%。

这项规定旨在解决来自贫困或混乱家庭的学生在完成家庭作业方面可能遇到的困难。但该政策不明确且自相矛盾。当然,不应布置学生无法独立完成或需要昂贵设备才能完成的家庭作业。但如果学区实质上是对那些因家庭生活复杂而不做家庭作业的学生网开一面,那就危险地接近于暗示需要为贫困儿童降低标准。

学区管理人员表示,家庭作业仍将是学校教育的一部分;教师可以随意布置任意数量的作业。但由于家庭作业在成绩中所占比重不超过10%,学生可以轻易跳过一半的家庭作业,而在成绩单上几乎看不出什么差别。有些学生可能不完成家庭作业也能在州考试中取得好成绩,但那些在考试中表现良好并完成了家庭作业的学生呢?家庭作业很可能起到了帮助作用。然而,该政策并没有授权教师找到最适合学生的方法,而是强加了一条一刀切的统一规则。

与此同时,该政策没有解决任何关于家庭作业的真正棘手问题。如果学区认为家庭作业对学生的学业成就不重要,就应该采取措施减少或取消作业,而不是让它们几乎不计分。相反,如果家庭作业很重要,它就应该占成绩的很大一部分。同时,该政策没有采取任何措施来确保学生收到的家庭作业是有意义的或适合他们的年龄和科目的,也没有确保教师布置的作业不超过他们愿意批改和纠正的数量。

家庭作业规定应该暂停执行,由负责制定教育政策的学校董事会调查此事并举行公开听证会。洛杉矶联合学区现在纠正家庭作业政策还为时不晚。

questions.q: It is implied in Paragraph 1 that nowadays homework____.
opts: is no longer an educational ritual
is not required for advanced courses
questions.explain: is receiving more criticism 正是 "如今作业更遭批评" 的标准同义表达，与预判完全一致。

questions.q: L.A. Unified has made the rule about homework mainly because poor students ____.
opts: tend to have moderate expectations for their education
have asked for a different educational standard
may have problems finishing their homework
have voiced their complaints about homework
questions.explain: may have problems finishing their homework 把 "贫困学生" "困难" "完成作业" 三要素与定位句一一对应，是定位句的标准同义改写。

questions.q: According to Paragraph 3, one problem with the policy is that it may____.
opts: result in students' indifference to their report cards
undermine the authority of state tests
questions.explain: discourage students from doing homework 是 students can easily skip half their homework 的标准同义替换——既然轻易跳过且成绩无变化，自然削弱了做作业的动力。

questions.q: As mentioned in Paragraph 4, a key question unanswered about homework is whether____.
opts: it places extra burdens on teachers
questions.explain: it counts much in schooling 是对 "作业是否重要/是否应该在成绩中占分量" 这一未解之问的高度概括，正中定位句对仗结构的核心变量。

questions.q: A suitable title for this text could be____.
opts: A Welcomed Policy for Poor Students
Wrong Interpretations of an Educational Policy
questions.explain: A Faulty Approach to Homework 在 "对象=作业政策"（Approach to Homework）与 "作者态度=否定"（Faulty）两个维度都与全文主线一致，是覆盖所有五段、不与任何段冲突的最佳概括。

title: 2012年真题 · Text 2
passage:
Pretty in pink: adult women do not remember being so obsessed with the colour, yet it is pervasive in our young girls' lives. It is not that pink is intrinsically bad, but it is such a tiny slice of the rainbow and, though it may celebrate girlhood in one way, it also repeatedly and firmly fuses girls' identity to appearance. Then it presents that connection, even among two-year-olds, between girls as not only innocent but as evidence of innocence. Looking around, I despaired at the singular lack of imagination about girls' lives and interests.

Girls' attraction to pink may seem unavoidable, somehow encoded in their DNA, but according to Jo Paoletti, an associate professor of American Studies, it is not. Children were not colour-coded at all until the early 20th century: in the era before domestic washing machines all babies wore white as a practical matter, since the only way of getting clothes clean was to boil them. What's more, both boys and girls wore what were thought of as gender-neutral dresses. When nursery colours were introduced, pink was actually considered the more masculine colour, a pastel version of red, which was associated with strength. Blue, with its intimations of the Virgin Mary, constancy and faithfulness, symbolised femininity. It was not until the mid-1980s, when amplifying age and sex differences became a dominant children's marketing strategy, that pink fully came into its own, when it began to seem inherently attractive to girls, part of what defined them as female, at least for the first few critical years.

I had not realised how profoundly marketing trends dictated our perception of what is natural to kids, including our core beliefs about their psychological development. Take the toddler. I assumed that phase was something experts developed after years of research into children's behaviour: wrong. Turns out, according to Daniel Cook, a historian of childhood consumerism, it was popularised as a marketing trick by clothing manufacturers in the 1930s.

Trade publications counselled department stores that, in order to increase sales, they should create a "third stepping stone" between infant wear and older kids' clothes. It was only after "toddler" became a common shoppers' term that it evolved into a broadly accepted developmental stage. Splitting kids, or adults, into ever-tinier categories has proved a sure-fire way to boost profits. And one of the easiest ways to segment a market is to magnify gender differences – or invent them where they did not previously exist.
passage_zh:
粉红色真美：成年女性并不记得自己曾如此痴迷于这种颜色，然而它却充斥在我们年幼女孩的生活中。粉红色本身并非坏事，但它只是彩虹中极小的一部分，尽管它可能在某种程度上赞颂女孩特质，但它也反复而坚定地将女孩的身份与外表融合在一起。然后它呈现出这种联系，甚至在两岁大的孩子中间，将女孩们之间的这种联系不仅视为纯真的表现，而且视为纯真本身的证据。环顾四周，我对女孩生活和兴趣方面想象力的极度匮乏感到绝望。

女孩对粉红色的喜爱似乎不可避免，仿佛编码在她们的DNA中，但根据美国研究副教授Jo Paoletti的说法，事实并非如此。直到20世纪初，儿童才开始按颜色区分：在家用洗衣机出现之前的时代，出于实际考虑，所有婴儿都穿白色衣服,因为清洗衣物的唯一方法是煮沸它们。而且，男孩和女孩都穿被认为是中性的连衣裙。当育儿室颜色被引入时，粉红色实际上被认为是更具男性气质的颜色，是红色的柔和版本，与力量相关联。蓝色则因其让人联想到圣母玛利亚、坚定和忠诚，象征着女性气质。直到20世纪80年代中期，当放大年龄和性别差异成为儿童市场营销的主导策略时，粉红色才真正确立了自己的地位，它开始似乎天然地吸引女孩，成为定义她们作为女性的一部分，至少在最初几年的关键时期是如此。

我没有意识到市场营销趋势如此深刻地影响了我们对儿童天性的认知，包括我们关于他们心理发展的核心信念。以学步儿童为例。我原以为这个阶段是专家们经过多年研究儿童行为后提出的：错了。事实证明,根据儿童消费主义历史学家Daniel Cook的说法，它是在20世纪30年代作为服装制造商的营销手段而流行起来的。

行业刊物建议百货商店，为了增加销售额，它们应该在婴儿装和大龄儿童服装之间创造一个"第三个阶梯"。只有在"学步儿童"成为购物者的常用术语之后，它才演变成一个被广泛接受的发展阶段。将儿童或成人划分为越来越细小的类别已被证明是提高利润的可靠方法。而细分市场最简单的方法之一就是放大性别差异——或者在以前不存在差异的地方创造出差异。

questions.q: By saying "it is…the rainbow" (Line 3, Para. 1), the author means pink ____.
opts: cannot explain girls' lack of imagination
should not be associated with girls' innocence
should not be the sole representation of girlhood
cannot influence girls' lives and interests
questions.explain: 预判"粉色不应独占代表女孩气质"与should not be the sole representation of girlhood字面对位，"sole"恰是"tiny slice"被放大成"全部"的反向表达，锁定C。

questions.q: According to Paragraph 2, which of the following is true of colours?
opts: Colours are encoded in girls' DNA.
Blue used to be regarded as the colour for girls.
Pink used to be a neutral colour in symbolising genders.
questions.explain: 预判"蓝色曾经=女性气质"与Blue used to be regarded as the colour for girls在时态（过去）与语义（蓝=女）两个维度完全对位，锁定B。

questions.q: The author suggests that our perception of children's psychological development was much influenced by ____.
opts: the marketing of products for children
questions.explain: 预判"营销趋势/儿童产品营销"直指the marketing of products for children，且后文toddler例证完全契合，锁定B。

questions.q: We may learn from Paragraph 4 that department stores were advised to_____.
opts: attach equal importance to different genders
focus on infant wear and older kids' clothes
questions.explain: 预判"细分消费群"与classify consumers into smaller groups字面对位，且原文紧接的通论句双重佐证，锁定A。

questions.q: It can be concluded that girls' attraction to pink seems to be ___.
opts: clearly explained by their inborn tendency
questions.explain: 全文主线"商业逐利→放大/制造性别差异→pink归属女孩"与mainly imposed by profit-driven businessmen在"施动方=逐利商家"与"动作=imposed"两层对位，锁定C。"mainly"对应"a dominant marketing strategy"中的"dominant"，留出空间不绝对化。

title: 2012年真题 · Text 3
passage:
In 2010, a federal judge shook America's biotech industry to its core. Companies had won patents for isolated DNA for decades – by 2005 some 20% of human genes were patented. But in March 2010 a judge ruled that genes were unpatentable. Executives were violently agitated. The Biotechnology Industry Organisation (BIO), a trade group, assured members that this was just a "preliminary step" in a longer battle.

On July 29th they were relieved, at least temporarily. A federal appeals court overturned the prior decision, ruling that Myriad Genetics could indeed hold patents to two genes that help forecast a woman's risk of breast cancer. The chief executive of Myriad, a company in Utah, said the ruling was a blessing to firms and patients alike.

But as companies continue their attempts at personalised medicine, the courts will remain rather busy. The Myriad case itself is probably not over. Critics make three main arguments against gene patents: a gene is a product of nature, so it may not be patented; gene patents suppress innovation rather than reward it; and patents' monopolies restrict access to genetic tests such as Myriad's. A growing number seem to agree. Last year a federal task-force urged reform for patents related to genetic tests. In October the Department of Justice filed a brief in the Myriad case, arguing that an isolated DNA molecule "is no less a product of nature…than are cotton fibres that have been separated from cotton seeds."

Despite the appeals court's decision, big questions remain unanswered. For example, it is unclear whether the sequencing of a whole genome violates the patents of individual genes within it. The case may yet reach the Supreme Court.

As the industry advances, however, other suits may have an even greater impact. Companies are unlikely to file many more patents for human DNA molecules – most are already patented or in the public domain. Firms are now studying how genes interact, looking for correlations that might be used to determine the causes of disease or predict a drug's efficacy. Companies are eager to win patents for "connecting the dots," explains Hans Sauer, a lawyer for the BIO.

Their success may be determined by a suit related to this issue, brought by the Mayo Clinic, which the Supreme Court will hear in its next term. The BIO recently held a convention which included sessions to coach lawyers on the shifting landscape for patents. Each meeting was packed.
passage_zh:
2010年,一位联邦法官的裁决震动了美国生物技术产业的核心。数十年来,各公司已经为分离的DNA赢得了专利——到2005年,约20%的人类基因已被授予专利。但在2010年3月,一位法官裁定基因不可授予专利。企业高管们极为震怒。生物技术产业组织(BIO)这一行业团体向其成员保证,这只是一场更长期战斗中的"初步阶段"。

7月29日,他们松了一口气,至少是暂时的。一家联邦上诉法院推翻了之前的裁决,裁定Myriad Genetics公司确实可以持有两个有助于预测女性乳腺癌风险的基因的专利。这家位于犹他州的公司的首席执行官表示,这一裁决对企业和患者都是一件幸事。

但随着各公司继续尝试个性化医疗,法院将依然相当繁忙。Myriad案件本身很可能尚未结束。批评者提出了反对基因专利的三个主要论点:基因是自然产物,因此不可授予专利;基因专利抑制创新而非奖励创新;专利的垄断限制了人们获得诸如Myriad的基因检测的机会。越来越多的人似乎表示赞同。去年,一个联邦工作组敦促改革与基因检测相关的专利。10月,司法部在Myriad案件中提交了一份简报,论证称分离的DNA分子"与从棉籽中分离出来的棉纤维一样,都是自然产物"。

尽管上诉法院作出了裁决,重大问题仍未得到解答。例如,对整个基因组进行测序是否侵犯了其中单个基因的专利尚不清楚。该案件可能最终会上诉至最高法院。

然而,随着该行业的发展,其他诉讼可能会产生更大的影响。各公司不太可能再为人类DNA分子申请更多专利——大多数已经获得专利或进入公共领域。企业现在正在研究基因如何相互作用,寻找可能用于确定疾病原因或预测药物疗效的相关性。BIO的律师Hans Sauer解释说,各公司渴望赢得"连接各点"的专利。

它们的成功可能取决于与此问题相关的一起诉讼,该诉讼由Mayo Clinic提起,最高法院将在下一任期审理此案。BIO最近举办了一次会议,其中包括指导律师应对专利格局变化的研讨会。每场会议都座无虚席。

questions.q: It can be learned from Paragraph 1 that the biotech companies would like____.
opts: the BIO to issue a warning
judges to rule out gene patenting
questions.explain: P1 既给出公司被裁定「激怒」的情绪反应，又给出 BIO「还要继续打」的态度表态，两条证据同指 genes to be patentable，故选 A。

questions.q: Those who are against gene patents believe that____.
opts: patents on genes depend much on innovation
courts should restrict access to genetic tests
questions.explain: 预判「自然产物不可专利」对应到选项 only man-made products are patentable，二者意思等价；其余两条论点（创新/检测）无相应选项，故锁定 B。

questions.q: According to Hans Sauer, companies are eager to win patents for____.
questions.explain: Hans Sauer 那句话中 connecting the dots 的具体内容在前一句被定义为 how genes interact，A 项 discovering gene interactions 正是此还原后的同义替换，故选 A。

questions.q: By saying "Each meeting was packed" (Line 4, Para. 6), the author means that ____.
opts: the BIO was a powerful organisation
gene patenting was a great concern
lawyers were keen to attend conventions
questions.explain: 把「packed」的现象义还原成「高度关注」的语境义，再用前句锁定关注对象为基因专利，正好等价于 gene patenting was a great concern。

questions.q: Generally speaking, the author's attitude toward gene patenting is ____.
questions.explain: 全文充分给两方话语权、并以「问题未决」收尾，作者本人无明显褒贬词，态度判定为客观，选 D。

title: 2012年真题 · Text 4
passage:
The great recession may be over, but this era of high joblessness is probably beginning. Before it ends, it will likely change the life course and character of a generation of young adults. And ultimately, it is likely to reshape our politics, our culture, and the character of our society for years.

No one tries harder than the jobless to find silver linings in this national economic disaster. Many said that unemployment, while extremely painful, had improved them in some ways: they had become less materialistic and more financially prudent; they were more aware of the struggles of others. In limited respects, perhaps the recession will leave society better off. At the very least, it has awoken us from our national fever dream of easy riches and bigger houses, and put a necessary end to an era of reckless personal spending.

But for the most part, these benefits seem thin, uncertain, and far off. In The Moral Consequences of Economic Growth, the economic historian Benjamin Friedman argues that both inside and outside the U.S., lengthy periods of economic stagnation or decline have almost always left society more mean-spirited and less inclusive, and have usually stopped or reversed the advance of rights and freedoms. Anti-immigrant sentiment typically increases, as does conflict between races and classes.

Income inequality usually falls during a recession, but it has not shrunk in this one. Indeed, this period of economic weakness may reinforce class divides, and decrease opportunities to cross them – especially for young people. The research of Till Von Wachter, the economist at Columbia University, suggests that not all people graduating into a recession see their life chances dimmed: those with degrees from elite universities catch up fairly quickly to where they otherwise would have been if they had graduated in better times; it is the masses beneath them that are left behind.

In the Internet age, it is particularly easy to see the resentment that has always been hidden within American society. More difficult, in the moment, is discerning precisely how these lean times are affecting society's character. In many respects, the U.S. was more socially tolerant entering this recession than at any time in its history, and a variety of national polls on social conflict since then have shown mixed results. We will have to wait and see exactly how these hard times will reshape our social fabric. But they certainly will reshape it, and all the more so the longer they extend.
passage_zh:
大衰退或许已经结束，但这个高失业率的时代可能才刚刚开始。在它结束之前，它很可能会改变一代年轻人的人生轨迹和性格特征。而且最终，它很可能在未来数年重塑我们的政治、我们的文化以及我们社会的特征。

没有人比失业者更努力地试图在这场全国性经济灾难中寻找一线希望。许多人说，失业虽然极其痛苦，但在某些方面改善了他们：他们变得不那么物质主义，在财务上更加审慎；他们更能意识到他人的挣扎。在有限的方面，也许这场衰退会让社会变得更好。至少，它把我们从轻松致富和更大房子的全民狂热梦想中唤醒，并给一个鲁莽的个人消费时代画上了必要的句号。

但在大多数情况下，这些好处似乎微薄、不确定且遥远。在《经济增长的道德后果》一书中，经济史学家Benjamin Friedman认为，无论在美国国内还是国外，漫长的经济停滞或衰退期几乎总是让社会变得更加刻薄、包容性更差，并且通常会阻止或逆转权利和自由的进步。反移民情绪通常会增加，种族和阶级之间的冲突也会增加。

收入不平等通常在经济衰退期间会下降，但在这次衰退中并未缩小。事实上，这段经济疲软时期可能会强化阶级分化，并减少跨越阶级的机会——尤其是对年轻人而言。Columbia University经济学家Till Von Wachter的研究表明，并非所有在经济衰退期毕业的人都会看到自己的人生机会变暗：那些拥有精英大学学位的人能相当快地赶上他们在较好时期毕业本应达到的位置；而被抛在后面的是他们之下的大众。

在互联网时代，特别容易看到一直隐藏在美国社会内部的怨恨。更困难的是，在当下准确辨别这些艰难时期如何影响社会性格。在许多方面，美国进入这次衰退时比其历史上任何时期都更具社会包容性，而此后关于社会冲突的各种全国性民调显示了好坏参半的结果。我们必须等待并观察这些艰难时期将如何重塑我们的社会结构。但它们肯定会重塑社会结构，而且持续时间越长，影响就越大。

questions.q: By saying "to find silver linings" (Line 1, Para. 2) the author suggests that the jobless try to____.
opts: make profits from the troubled economy
look on the bright side of the recession
questions.explain: 预判 "在坏事里找好处" 与 look on the bright side of the recession 完全对齐，silver linings 即 bright side 的英语成语化表达。

questions.q: According to Paragraph 2, the recession has made people ____.

title: 2012年真题 · 完形填空
passage:
Millions of Americans and foreigners see G.I. Joe as a mindless war toy, the symbol of American military adventurism, but that's not how it used to be. To the men and women who __(1)__ in World War II and the people they liberated, the G.I. was the __(2)__ man grown into hero, the poor farm kid torn away from his home, the guy who __(3)__ all the burdens of battle, who slept in cold foxholes, who went without the __(4)__ of food and shelter, who stuck it out and drove back the Nazi reign of murder. This was not a volunteer soldier, not someone well paid, __(5)__ an average guy, up __(6)__ the best trained, best equipped, fiercest, most brutal enemies seen in centuries.

His name isn't much. G.I. is just a military abbreviation __(7)__ Government Issue, and it was on all of the articles __(8)__ to soldiers. And Joe? A common name for a guy who never __(9)__ it to the top. Joe Blow, Joe Palooka, Joe Magrac…a working class name. The United States has __(10)__ had a president or vice-president or secretary of state Joe.

G.I. Joe had a __(11)__ career fighting German, Japanese, and Korean troops. He appears as a character, or a __(12)__ of American personalities, in the 1945 movie The Story of G.I. Joe, based on the last days of war correspondent Ernie Pyle. Some of the soldiers Pyle __(13)__ portrayed themselves in the film. Pyle was famous for covering the __(14)__ side of the war, writing about the dirt-snow-and-mud soldiers, not how many miles were __(15)__ or what towns were captured or liberated. His reports __(16)__ the "Willie" cartoons of famed Stars and Stripes artist Bill Mauldin. Both men __(17)__ the dirt and exhaustion of war, the __(18)__ of civilization that the soldiers shared with each other and the civilians: coffee, tobacco, whiskey, shelter, sleep. __(19)__ Egypt, France, and a dozen more countries, G.I. Joe was any American soldier, __(20)__ the most important person in their lives.
passage_zh:
数百万美国人和外国人将G.I. Joe视为一个无思想的战争玩具,是美国军事冒险主义的象征,但它过去并非如此。对于在二战中服役的男女军人以及他们解放的人民而言,G.I.是成长为英雄的普通人,是被迫离开家园的贫苦农家子弟,是承受战斗所有重负的人,是睡在冰冷散兵坑里的人,是缺少食物和住所等生活必需品的人,是坚持到底并击退纳粹杀戮统治的人。这不是志愿兵,不是报酬丰厚的人,而是普通人,面对的却是几个世纪以来训练最精良、装备最精良、最凶猛、最残暴的敌人。

他的名字并不起眼。G.I.只是一个军事缩写,意思是Government Issue(政府配发),它出现在发给士兵的所有物品上。那Joe呢?一个从未出人头地的普通人的常见名字。Joe Blow、Joe Palooka、Joe Magrac……一个工人阶级的名字。美国从未有过一位名叫Joe的总统、副总统或国务卿。

G.I. Joe在与德国、日本和朝鲜军队的作战中有着卓越的战绩。他作为一个角色,或者说一组美国人的性格集合,出现在1945年的电影《G.I. Joe的故事》中,该片基于战地记者Ernie Pyle的最后战地岁月。Pyle采访过的一些士兵在影片中扮演他们自己。Pyle以报道战争的人性面而闻名,他书写的是那些满身尘土、冰雪和泥泞的士兵,而不是推进了多少英里或占领或解放了哪些城镇。他的报道与著名《星条旗报》艺术家Bill Mauldin的"Willie"漫画相呼应。两人都强调战争的肮脏和疲惫,强调士兵们彼此之间以及与平民分享的文明碎片:咖啡、烟草、威士忌、住所、睡眠。对于埃及、法国和其他十几个国家来说,G.I. Joe就是任何一名美国士兵,在那个时刻是他们生命中最重要的人。

blanks.explain: 词义辨析：后文紧接 "the people they liberated"，说明这些人是参战并解放他人的盟军士兵。正解：serve in WWII = 在二战中服役/参战，与 liberated 完全相容
词义辨析：下文用 "穷苦农家娃""普通人" 一连串同位语为这个形容词作注脚。正解：common man 即"平民、普通人"，与下文 average guy 完全同义复述
固定搭配：本句平行结构 "slept in cold foxholes... went without food and shelter... stuck it out" 全是"扛下苦难"。正解：bear the burden 是固定搭配，意为"承担重负"
词义辨析：went without 直接点明"连最基本的都没"，定位"必需品"。正解：necessities of life 是固定表达，指生活必需品
逻辑关系：本句构成 "not X, not Y, but Z" 的经典对比结构。正解：not...not...but... 经典对比结构，引出真正描述
固定搭配：短语 be up against = 面对/对抗（强敌）。正解：up against 是固定短语，意为"面对/对抗（强敌或难题）"
词义辨析：主语是 abbreviation（缩写），缩写=A 代表 B 的对应关系。正解：meaning = 即……，直接给出全称释义
词义辨析：前文说 Government Issue（政府配发），物品的去向是"发给士兵"。正解：hand out = 分发，恰与 Government Issue 同义
固定搭配：下句"美国从没有 Joe 当总统"反向印证"没爬上去"。正解：make it to the top 是"出人头地、做到顶层"的固定表达
逻辑关系：上句 never 已定否定基调。正解：never 续上句否定，且 has never had 是常见句法
词义辨析：全文称颂基调 + "对抗德日韩三国军队"暗含"战功卓著"。正解：distinguished career = 卓越职业生涯（固定搭配）
词义辨析：前文 "as a character, or a ___ of personalities" 的 or 提示"或一种聚合"。正解：a collection of personalities = 多种人物形象的集合
词义辨析：上文已点明 Pyle 是 "war correspondent"（战地记者）。正解：interview 正是记者的专业动作=采访
词义辨析：紧随的 "not how many miles were ___ or what towns were captured" 排除军事面。正解：human side = 战争的人性面/人的故事
固定搭配：平行项 "towns were captured or liberated" 提示军事推进语义。正解：gain miles/ground = 推进，攻占的英里
词义辨析：下句 "Both men emphasized the dirt and exhaustion of war..." 明示两人主题相同。正解：parallel = 与……相似/并行，呼应 Both men 同向归纳
词义辨析：上句确认两人方向一致 + 上一空已定"写战争人性面"。正解：emphasize = 强调，呼应两人"突出战争人性面"
词义辨析：冒号后只列"咖啡、烟、威士忌、住处、睡眠"等零碎日常。正解：fragments of civilization = 文明的零星片段
固定搭配：末句 "the most important person in their lives" 中 their 指这些国家的人。正解：To + 国家 = 对……来说
逻辑关系：全文反复对比 "现在 vs 当年"，本句要锁定"当年那时"。正解：at that point = 在那个时点（即二战时期）

title: 2012年真题 · 新题型（多项对应）
intro: Read the following text and match each of the numbered items in the left column to its corresponding information in the right column. There are two extra choices in the right column. (10 points)
titles: A. emphasized the virtue of classical heroes.
B. highlighted the public glory of the leading artists.
C. focused on epochal figures whose lives were hard to imitate.
D. opened up new realms of understanding the great men in history.
E. held that history should be the story of the masses and their record of struggle.
F. dismissed virtue as unnecessary for successful leaders.
G. depicted the worthy lives of engineers, industrialists and explorers.

paras.explain: 锚点：彼特拉克突出古典英雄的美德；依据：主张与A逐字对应
锚点：马基雅维利认为美德对成功领导者并不必要；依据：弃美德=dismissed virtue
锚点：斯迈尔斯描绘工程师、实业家、探险家的可敬人生；依据：对象三类人逐字吻合
锚点：卡莱尔聚焦人生难以效仿的划时代人物；依据：epochal+hard to imitate双锁定
锚点：马恩认为历史应是大众及其斗争的记录；依据：近乎原句搬运

passage:
"Universal history, the history of what man has accomplished in this world, is at bottom the History of the Great Men who have worked here," wrote the Victorian sage Thomas Carlyle. Well, not any more it is not.

Suddenly, Britain looks to have fallen out with its favorite historical form. This could be no more than a passing literary craze, but it also points to a broader truth about how we now approach the past: less concerned with learning from our forefathers and more interested in feeling their pain. Today, we want empathy, not inspiration.

From the earliest days of the Renaissance, the writing of history meant recounting the exemplary lives of great men. In 1337, Petrarch began work on his rambling writing De Viris Illustribus – On Famous Men, highlighting the virtus (or virtue) of classical heroes. Petrarch celebrated their greatness in conquering fortune and rising to the top. This was the biographical tradition which Niccolò Machiavelli turned on its head. In The Prince, he championed cunning, ruthlessness, and boldness, rather than virtue, mercy and justice, as the skills of successful leaders.

Over time, the attributes of greatness shifted. The Romantics commemorated the leading painters and authors of their day, stressing the uniqueness of the artist's personal experience rather than public glory. By contrast, the Victorian author Samuel Smiles wrote Self-Help as a catalogue of the worthy lives of engineers, industrialists and explorers. "The valuable examples which they furnish of the power of self-help, of patient purpose, resolute working, and steadfast integrity, issuing in the formation of truly noble and manly character, exhibit," wrote Smiles, "what it is in the power of each to accomplish for himself." His biographies of James Watt, Richard Arkwright and Josiah Wedgwood were held up as beacons to guide the working man through his difficult life.

This was all a bit bourgeois for Thomas Carlyle, who focused his biographies on the truly heroic lives of Martin Luther, Oliver Cromwell and Napoleon Bonaparte. These epochal figures represented lives hard to imitate, but to be acknowledged as possessing higher authority than mere mortals.

Not everyone was convinced by such bombast. "The history of all hitherto existing society is the history of class struggles," wrote Marx and Engels in The Communist Manifesto. For them, history did nothing, it possessed no immense wealth nor waged battles: "It is man, real, living man who does all that." And history should be the story of the masses and their record of struggle. As such, it needed to appreciate the economic realities, the social contexts and power relations in which each epoch stood. For: "Men make their own history, but they do not make it just as they please; they do not make it under circumstances chosen by themselves, but under circumstances directly found, given and transmitted from the past."

This was the tradition which revolutionised our appreciation of the past. In place of Thomas Carlyle, Britain nurtured Christopher Hill, EP Thompson and Eric Hobsbawm. History from below stood alongside biographies of great men. Whole new realms of understanding – from gender to race to cultural studies – were opened up as scholars unpicked the multiplicity of lost societies. And it transformed public history too: downstairs became just as fascinating as upstairs.
passage_zh:
维多利亚时代的智者托马斯·卡莱尔写道："世界历史，即人类在这个世界上所成就之事的历史，归根结底是在此奋斗的伟人的历史。"然而，如今情况已不再如此。

突然之间,英国似乎与其最钟爱的历史叙述形式决裂了。这也许只是一时的文学风潮,但它也指向了一个关于我们如今如何看待过去的更广泛的真相:我们不再关注从先辈那里汲取教训,而是更感兴趣于感受他们的痛苦。今天,我们要的是共情,而非激励。

从文艺复兴最早期开始,历史书写就意味着讲述伟人的典范生活。1337年,彼特拉克开始撰写其漫长的著作《名人传》,突出古典英雄的美德。彼特拉克赞颂他们征服命运、登上巅峰的伟大之处。正是这一传记传统被尼科洛·马基雅维利彻底颠覆。在《君主论》中,他推崇狡诈、无情和大胆,而非美德、仁慈和正义,将其视为成功领导者的技能。

随着时间推移,伟大的特质发生了转变。浪漫主义者颂扬当时杰出的画家和作家,强调艺术家个人体验的独特性而非公众荣耀。相比之下,维多利亚时代作家塞缪尔·斯迈尔斯将《自助》写成工程师、实业家和探险家高尚生活的汇编。斯迈尔斯写道:"他们所提供的关于自助之力、坚韧目标、坚定工作和坚贞正直的宝贵范例,展现了真正高尚而刚毅品格的形成,说明每个人都有能力为自己成就些什么。"他为詹姆斯·瓦特、理查德·阿克赖特和乔赛亚·韦奇伍德所作的传记被奉为指引工人阶级度过艰难人生的灯塔。

这一切对托马斯·卡莱尔来说有些过于资产阶级化了,他的传记聚焦于马丁·路德、奥利弗·克伦威尔和拿破仑·波拿巴真正英雄般的人生。这些划时代人物代表着难以效仿的生命,但应被承认拥有高于凡人的权威。

并非所有人都被这种夸张言辞所说服。"迄今为止一切社会的历史都是阶级斗争的历史,"马克思和恩格斯在《共产党宣言》中写道。对他们而言,历史什么也不做,它既不拥有巨大财富也不发动战争:"做这一切的是人,是现实的、活生生的人。"而历史应该是大众及其斗争记录的故事。因此,它需要理解每个时代所处的经济现实、社会语境和权力关系。因为:"人们自己创造自己的历史,但是他们并不是随心所欲地创造,并不是在他们自己选定的条件下创造,而是在直接碰到的、既定的、从过去承继下来的条件下创造。

正是这一传统革新了我们对过去的理解。英国培养出了克里斯托弗·希尔、E.P.汤普森和埃里克·霍布斯鲍姆,取代了托马斯·卡莱尔。自下而上的历史与伟人传记并驾齐驱。随着学者们剖析失落社会的多样性,从性别到种族再到文化研究,全新的理解领域被开辟出来。这也改变了公共历史:楼下变得和楼上一样引人入胜。

title: 2012年真题 · 翻译
passage:
When people in developing countries worry about migration, they are usually concerned at the prospect of their best and brightest departure to Silicon Valley or to hospitals and universities in the developed world. These are the kind of workers that countries like Britain, Canada and Australia try to attract by using immigration rules that privilege college graduates.

Lots of studies have found that well-educated people from developing countries are particularly likely to emigrate. A big survey of Indian households in 2004 found that nearly 40% of emigrants had more than a high-school education, compared with around 3.3% of all Indians over the age 25. This "brain drain" has long bothered policymakers in poor countries. They fear that it hurts their economies, depriving them of much-needed skilled workers who could have taught at their universities, worked in their hospitals and come up with clever new products for their factories to make.
passage_zh:
当发展中国家的人们担忧人口外流时，他们所担心的通常是这样一种前景：自己国家最优秀的人才会流向硅谷，或流向发达国家的医院和大学。这些人才正是英国、加拿大、澳大利亚等国想方设法吸引的对象，为此这些国家专门制定了向大学毕业生倾斜的移民政策。

大量研究发现，来自发展中国家、受过良好教育的人尤其倾向于移居国外。2004 年针对印度家庭开展的一项大规模调查发现，移民中近 40% 的人拥有高中以上学历，而 25 岁以上的印度人总体中受过同等教育的仅约 3.3%。长期以来，这种「人才流失」一直困扰着贫穷国家的政策制定者。他们（这些政策制定者）担心人才流失会损害本国经济，使本国失去亟需的技术工人——这些工人本来可以在本国大学执教、在本国医院工作，还可以为本国工厂研发出新颖巧妙的产品。
